<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Large offshore wind farms may modulate clouds and precipitation by extracting momentum and altering boundary layer mixing. We assess the modeled precipitation response to activating a wind farm parameterization (WFP) in the WRF model over the Southern Bight of the North Sea using three years of 1 km simulations (2021–2023) with paired runs that differ only by WFP inclusion. Annual maps show localized, spatially compensating anomalies, with positive differences over and around major arrays and negative differences downstream, yielding near-zero domain-mean changes. A permutation test indicates statistically significant signals over larger wind farm clusters. Conditioning by domain-mean hub-height wind direction highlights a sectoral dependence, with the most coherent, flow-aligned pattern for South-West inflow. Further conditioning by wind speed reveals a nonlinear response, which is most pronounced for intermediate to strong winds. Vertical velocity differences align with these precipitation patterns (updrafts near farm arrays, subsidence downstream). These results describe a modeled precipitation response to wind farms rather than validated real-world impacts and motivate targeted observations and sensitivity studies.</jats:p>
title: Precipitation response to wind farms represented in WRF over the Southern Bight of the North Sea
